Hi Karthik,

Quick one — we expect a product-driven spike and need to add ~150k token-units/month starting July 1. Current contract runs through 2027-12-31. Procurement asked whether we can: (a) co-term the new add with our analytics vendor (same fiscal year-end) or (b) annualize now (pay for 12 months upfront) for a blended discount.

Two constraints: our PO team needs an invoice schedule (they prefer a single annual invoice if possible) and legal needs a clear amendment to review (we can turn quickly but need 5 business days).

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can offer two practical paths and a hybrid. High level below; attached is a one-pager with numbers and an editable proration workbook.

Option A — Staggered uplift (preferred if you want to minimize cash outlay):
- Add 150k token-units starting 2026-07-01.
- We apply an uplift discount band of 8% on the incremental volume for the remaining months of your contract; we also issue a "staircase credit" equal to 60% of the uplift to smooth billing into the next invoice cycle.
- Billing: monthly invoices for the incremental usage, with a single annual reconciliation invoice at contract anniversary to true-up.

Option B — Immediate annualization (clean invoice):
- Annualize the added capacity now (12 months committed) at a 10% one-time discount on the annualized incremental spend.
- Billing: single annual invoice (one line item) payable on signature. Co-term: we keep existing contract term but treat incremental capacity as an annual commitment that renews on the same cadence.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Option A keeps cash near-term lower but requires a small reconciliation at anniversary. Option B gets procurement the single invoice they prefer and yields a slightly better discount.
- Legal: both require a lightweight amendment. For Option B we will need sign-off from Legal for the annualized amendment; Option A can be executed with an SOW + amendment.
- Timeline: We can prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment within 48 hours for Option B if we get a green light.

Attachments: granularai-uplift-proposal.pdf (quote + sample invoice), proration-sample.xlsx (monthly math).

If you want, we can also do a hybrid: annualize 50% of the uplift for a mid-level discount and leave 50% staggered.

Proposed next step: pick Option A, B, or Hybrid and confirm procurement timing — I’ll loop in Legal (Olga) and Naomi (ops) to draft the amendment and invoice schedule.

Cheers,

Adding a quick ops view so procurement has concrete numbers to work with. Example proration for Option A (assuming contract end 2027-12-31 and add starts 2026-07-01):

- Incremental monthly list price: $12,500 (150k token-units * unit rate)
- 8% uplift discount applied to incremental line -> $11,500/month (rounded)
- Staircase credit: we apply a one-time credit of $23,000 (60% of projected 6-month incremental spend) spread over next invoice to smooth impact.

Sample invoice schedule (Option A):
- July through December 2026: monthly invoices at $11,500 for incremental line item.
- 2027-01-01: reconciliation invoice showing true-up vs credits (single line).

If procurement insists on one invoice now (Option B):
- Total annualized incremental spend = $12,500 * 12 = $150,000
- 10% annualization discount = $15,000 -> invoice = $135,000 due on signature

I attached a quick proration workbook so you can drop in your exact unit rate and term to see the schedule. Legal (Olga) — if we proceed with Option B, we’ll need an amendment template and a DocuSign wrapper.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to walk procurement through the math.
